name: Kangchenjunga
fa_by: Joe Brown & George Band (1955 British expedition, from Nepal)
status_note: Main summit on the Sikkim–Nepal border. Sikkim treats it as sacred and banned climbing in 2001; the Indian-side route has been closed since c.2000 and in 2019 IMF said it would not issue permits for Sikkim's sacred peaks. Routinely climbed from Nepal; by tradition summiteers stop just short of the true top (1955 promise to the Chogyal of Sikkim).
grade_note: 8,000 m expedition with objective hazards; all normal routes are from Nepal
base: Yuksom (Indian side, trekking only to Goecha La) / Taplejung (Nepal)
notable: India's highest peak and world's 3rd highest; second ascent 1977 by an Indian Army team (Col. Narendra Kumar) via the NE spur from Sikkim.

name: Nanda Devi
fa_by: Bill Tilman & Noel Odell (British-American expedition)
status_note: Nanda Devi Sanctuary and main summit closed to climbers and locals since 1983 (one-off 1993 army clean-up). Feb 2026 Uttarakhand opening of 83 peaks named Nanda Devi East, not the main summit.
grade_note: Guarded by the Rishi Gorge and sanctuary wall; south (Coxcomb) ridge is technical rock/snow/ice
notable: Highest peak entirely within India; 1936 ascent was the highest summit climbed until 1950.

name: Zemu Gap Peak
status_note: Wikipedia: one of the highest unclimbed named peaks, no known attempts. Low-prominence subsidiary of the Kangchenjunga massif; height uncertain.
notable: A subsidiary summit of the Kangchenjunga massif rather than an independent mountain; no known attempts.

name: Kamet
fa_by: Frank Smythe, Eric Shipton, R.L. Holdsworth & Lewa Sherpa
status_note: Open via IMF/Uttarakhand (included in Feb 2026 list of 83 peaks with fee waivers); inner-line border area near Tibet.
grade_note: Relatively straightforward snow/ice route for its height but a full high-altitude expedition
notable: First peak over 25,000 ft ever climbed (1931).

name: Saltoro Kangri

base: Siachen Base Camp (Nubra) – army access only
notable: Highest peak in Ladakh (on the AGPL); India also claims K2 (8,611 m) in Pakistan-administered Gilgit-Baltistan.

notable: Highest peak entirely within Ladakh (Indian-administered).
